thread:
laura_sales: Hi folks — health-tech POC asking for a short connectivity playbook. Their checklist: preserve client IP for audit logs, allow TLS-inspect boxes in the middle, clarify SNI rewrite impact on cert pinning/mTLS, and a clear list of egress IPs/FQDNs for their firewall team. Also want cost comparison PrivateLink vs peering for a 2-week POC.

andy_netops: Quick summary: 
- VPC Peering: preserves source IP end-to-end, low latency, needs cross-account peering and route table edits. No hourly endpoint fee but potential data transfer charges depending on AZ/region.
- Interface PrivateLink: faster to provision, provides endpoint ENIs in the customer's subnet, often results in source-NAT to endpoint EIP unless you front with a proxy. There is an hourly endpoint fee and per-GB data processing.
- TLS inspection: possible with either topology, but breaking SNI or mTLS on the wire requires you to terminate TLS at your inspection layer. If you rewrite SNI, cert pinning/mTLS will be impacted.

jun_infra: POC recommendation (2 lightweight options to propose to customer):
1) PrivateLink + small NLB + reverse proxy in their VPC: easiest onboarding, preserves client identity in X-Forwarded-For. Good for teams that can accept header-based identity.
2) Cross-account VPC Peering + SGs + routing: preserves client src IP natively. Best if they need src-based ACLs or IP-based auditing.

maya_sales_eng: They specifically asked: "If we use PrivateLink, can you give us the exact IPs to allow on our perimeter firewall?"

andy_netops: For PrivateLink we give one or more EIPs per endpoint (region-specific) for POC. For peering, nothing to allow inbound since traffic routes internally, but their NAT/egress will hit our public egress IPs if they go out to the hosted API. Example allowlist snippet below.

security_ops: Security note: For regulated PHI workflows, we do not recommend terminating customer-originating mTLS inside our hosted shared tenancy unless we have a signed DPA addendum and enable a dedicated Private deployment. Otherwise advise terminating mTLS at the customer edge and using app-level auth to our API.

laura_sales: Andy, can you paste a short firewall snippet I can hand to their NetOps? Keep it copy/paste friendly.

andy_netops: Sure — example for an enterprise NGFW (replace placeholders):
```
# OUTBOUND allowlist for Redwood POC (example)
# Replace <REDFW_EIP_1> with EIP(s) we provide for the PrivateLink endpoint
allow tcp from 10.10.0.0/16 to <REDFW_EIP_1> 443
allow tcp from 10.10.0.0/16 to <REDFW_EIP_2> 443  # additional EIP if provided
# If using PrivateLink interface endpoints, ensure the customer's subnet route to the ENI is allowed
# NTP if needed
allow udp from 10.10.0.0/16 to <REDFW_EIP_1> 123
```

jun_infra: Add this note: if their TLS inspector needs to see the destination hostname (SNI) for routing, they must not TLS-terminate after an opaque proxy rewrites SNI. If they plan to rewrite SNI you should probably do peering or a dedicated tunnel instead.

maya_sales_eng: Short bullets on client IP preservation I can email?

andy_netops: Client IP options (short):
- VPC Peering: native src-IP preserved to our backend.
- PrivateLink + reverse proxy/NLB: preserve client via X-Forwarded-For header.
- Proxy Protocol v2: supported for Dedicated & Private deployments to pass original TCP src.

security_ops: Callout: proxy-protocol and dedicated passthrough are not available on the shared public-hosted API. If they need guaranteed src-IP passthrough and auditing, Dedicated or Peering is required.

laura_sales: They also want cost guidance for a 2-week POC (rough line-item). Can we give a 2-3 line estimate they can use for internal approval?

andy_netops: Rough POC cost guidance (estimate):
- PrivateLink: Endpoint hours (~$0.02-$0.05/hr depending on region) + data processing per GB (~$0.01-$0.05/GB). For light testing (100 GB) expect ~$10-100 in data fees + small endpoint hours.
- Peering: no endpoint-hour fee, but if cross-AZ/regional traffic occurs, data transfer costs may be comparable. Expect similar ballpark for 100 GB depending on AZ layout.
- Dedicated: if they want proxy-protocol or dedicated SLA, needs capacity reservation — likely monthly commitment, not ideal for a 2-week POC unless they agree to a short pilot fee.

jun_infra: Operational notes for their NetOps:
- If they want source-IP-based firewall rules on our side, prefer peering or Dedicated.
- If they can accept XFF, PrivateLink + proxy is simplest and fastest.
- Provide the endpoint EIP(s) 24-48 hrs before cutover so they can populate rules.

maya_sales_eng: Anything to add about SNI rewrite and cert pinning?

security_ops: If cert pinning or mTLS validation is in use, advise them to terminate at the customer proxy and use token-based or mTLS reauth to our backend, or request a dedicated Private deployment where we can configure mutual TLS properly.

deploy-bot: Runbook update: privatelink-onboarding v2.0 -> https://redwood.example.com/internal/runbooks/privatelink-onboarding :white_check_mark:

laura_sales: Awesome, I'll send this to the customer along with the allowlist snippet and a 2-line cost note. Will follow up with SOC questionnaire items when available. Thanks all :pray:
